decisions.reason: The materials management module extends the established practice-management software, the firm has already invested development effort in it, and it supports the announced push toward integrated, paperless clinics, so management would likely blame any modest early uptake on a normal ramp-up rather than drop it.

The secure KIM messaging service is publicly featured on its own page, is tied to mandatory telematics infrastructure and the firm's health-IT direction, and has received further investment through the KIM 1.5 update, so commitment is high and dropping it is very unlikely.
